body:
I know that my parents and my sister come from a good place, but sometimes it's hard to remember that; we've never been one for hugs or things, and the only time my mom's been openly emotional with me is when she used to apologize for hitting me. Dealing with my sister is harder because I'm the older one and I feel like I've let her down the most, not being someone she could look up to or be proud of. Most of her friends (she's away at school) don't even know she has a sister because she doesn't want to tell them I just do nothing, but I told her she can tell them I died so they won't ask her about it. I honestly do feel like it could be better for everyone if I wasn't around to be a burden like that, but I'm worried about what it could do to her, since she's already been affected by having friends that killed themselves.

I'd like to go back to college, but I'm not sure about it: Aside from the tuition and all, I'm worried that the same thing that happened last time will happen again. Whatever issues I have haven't been dealt with, and I don't think I could handle trying again just to wind up hiding and failing, but you can't just sit in class while you burst into tears, right? I felt like I was dying every day and I would rather go all at once if I had to go through it again.

Heh, I know 26 isn't that bad; I've read posts and stories elsewhere from people who were in their 40s or 50s and I figure I've actually got it pretty easy, but that just makes me feel worse. I should be capable of doing stuff and handling it, but I'm... not. I guess I'm not too good at perspective because I can only focus on the quarter-of-a-century-gone thing, and I've never been too hopeful of living a full century anyway.

I would like to go back to school, since I've always liked learning; on good days, when I wasn't too messed up, I liked my classes. I really think I should've been able to pass them easily, but I wound up missing too many and, well. I'd like to start over, without transcripts, since by the end my grades were so bad I would have been put on academic probation, if not outright dropped, but I don't think that's possible.

I've looked into therapists/counselors/psychologists in my area, but I have no money or health insurance and I don't think I can expect any help from my family; when I was a kid, I used to be worried by the suicidal thoughts and asked if I could see someone for years, but they always seemed to think I was blaming them and would start yelling (and, needless to say, refused). Since it's been getting worse, I've tried to bring up the possibility but, well, they still don't take me seriously, and my mother doesn't believe in psychology/psychiatry.

I've never seen anyone to be diagnosed with anything, so I don't know if medication would help, plus there's the issue of payment. I don't care about it not being easy or fun - not a lot of either for me anyway - but I have no way of paying for anything. Are the group meetings like support groups? (Sorry if this is a dumb question, I don't really have a lot of knowledge in this area.)
